pn:
Dhotaka. One of Bāvarī’s disciples; he was among those who visited the Buddha at Bāvarī’s request (Snp. p.194). The questions he asked of the Buddha on this occasion, and the answers given, are found in the Dhotakamāṇavapucchā. SN, p.204f; explained at Snp-a (ii.592f.) and also CNid. (19ff.). He became an Arahant.

In the time of Padumuttara Buddha he was a Brahmin teacher named Chalaṅga, with a large following, and he built a bridge over the Bhagīrathī for the Buddha and his monks to cross in comfort. Ap.ii.343ff.

[ cf BHS dhovana, S. dhāvana], 1. rinsing, washing; washing off ; Vin V 174, 27 (~ena vicāraṇena chedanena …); A I 277, 15 (udakaṃ ṭhapetvā pādānaṃ ~āya); It 111, 4* (ucchādanena nhāpanena pādānaṃ ~ena ca); Sp 1308, 33 (~aṃ ca paṭiggaho ti aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā purāṇacīvaradhovāpanaṃ ca cīvarapaṭiggahaṇaṃ ca); Mp III 49, 25 (yena kenaci dhovanūpakena udakena ~aṃ udakasantoso nāma); Pj II 375, 19 (saṅghāṭirajassa ~aṃ); — ifc see kāsāva-, cīvara-, patta- ( sv patta 3 ); — 2. water for washing ; Vin I 342, 30 (icchati … khaggānaṃ ca ~aṃ pātuṃ); M III 155, 3 (āsanaṃ paññāpesi udakaṃ ca pādānaṃ ~aṃ, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee omit ~aṃ); — ifc see ukkhali-, thāli- ( sv thālī ), patta- ( sv patta 3 ), mukha-, sarāva-, hattha-; — 3. dhovanā f. [ from dhovati], (an instrument for) washing ; Vin IV 262, 27 (udakasuddhikaṃ nāma muttakaraṇassa ~ā vuccati).
NCP: neuter rinsing, washing; washing off. water for washing. (according to commentaries) a certain ritual (and festival), involving washing of bones.
